material_preparation: Naturally infected 1-3-month-old goat kids of approximately 10 kg were randomized to five groups of eight; the A. absinthium group received one oral dose of ethanolic aerial-part extract at 2 g/kg body weight.

primary_outcome: At 1.0% solution, A. absinthium produced 85.5 +/- 16.5% mortality in S. papillosus L1-2 versus 1.5 +/- 3.4% in control, but only 19.4 +/- 6.7% in S. papillosus L3 and 0.0 +/- 0.0% in H. contortus L3.
host_control_or_selectivity: Distilled-water negative controls, albendazole positive controls, five replicates, and the 46-plant comparison were reported; no in-vivo host, residue, or mammalian selectivity endpoint was included.
constituent_attribution: The result is a stage-specific, qualitative wormwood tincture phenotype; it does not establish a causal volatile, sesquiterpene lactone, or vermifuge dose in an animal.
remaining_eligibility_gate: Voucher/chemotype confirmation, constituent-resolved fractionation, adult-worm and in-vivo efficacy, host selectivity, residue limits, and independent replication remain open.
